measurements.note: Method and load from the label: the sheet prints "HDT A", which ISO 75 defines as 1.8 MPa (D65). Flagged physically implausible: the sheet prints a heat deflection at 1.8 MPa of 93 °C for a PETG-CF, above PETG's glass transition; an amorphous polymer's HDT does not pass its Tg. The sheet prints it in its Injection column. Kept as printed; it backs nothing. Corrected against the source: the table is headed "Properties FDM H Injection Method", and this row's one value stands in the Injection column (page image): an injection-moulded bar.

measurements.note: Flagged physically implausible: this undated revision prints a specific gravity of 1.19 g/cc for a PETG "reinforced with 20%... carbon fibres"; neat PETG is 1.22 to 1.30 g/cm³ and carbon fibre about 1.8, so 20 % of it gives about 1.35, and no carbon-fibre PETG is lighter than plain PETG. The 2024 revision (R-FORMFUTURA-SB-20261018-7b525961687e) prints 1,32 for its 15 % fibre, and is the product's. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.

measurements.note: Flagged physically implausible: the sheet prints a density of 1,1 g/cm3 for "a highly modified, carbon fibre-additivated amorphous PET copolymer". Carbon fibre (about 1.8 g/cm³) makes a compound denser than its resin, and neat PETG is 1.22 to 1.30 g/cm³ (polymers.csv), so a carbon-fibre PETG cannot weigh 1.1; the sheet gives one significant figure and no fibre content. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.

measurements.note: The row's condition reads "Charpy notched 23°C" and the method it names, ISO 179-1eU, is ISO 179's unnotched (edgewise) designation; the sheet's own word for the notch is kept and the row is held back, as Extrudr's rows whose label and standard disagree on the notch are.

The row is labelled "Flexural modulus" and cites ISO 527-1, the tensile test's standard, not ISO 178 or ASTM D790; the sheet's earlier revision printed a tensile modulus (9495 MPa) and no flexural one, and this one leaves its "Tensile modulus" row empty. Which modulus the 4250 MPa is cannot be read from the page, and the two differ on a printed bar, so the row is held back and backs nothing (screening build C14, D149).
